At DevDay Exchange 2026 in Berlin, OpenAI mostly rehashed announcements it had already made in San Francisco. A few new details came out about the European launch of Dots, Codex usage, and the Q&A session.

Romain Huet, OpenAI's head of developer experience, said the AI assistant Dots should become more widely available in Europe "in a few weeks" following talks with regulators. Personal Pro accounts in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the UK are still locked out of the service. Certain business accounts can already get access.

In Germany, weekly active Codex users have grown twentyfold since January 2026, according to OpenAI. Back in June, we reported a more than sevenfold increase based on the company's own figures. OpenAI again didn't share absolute numbers. The company says nearly one in five desktop users taps skills for documents, presentations, or spreadsheets, which means they're using the coding tool for general office work.

During the Q&A, someone asked why OpenAI still doesn't offer a model that understands video sequences the way Google's Gemini does. Management said customers have barely asked for it. So the company hasn't prioritized the feature beyond single-frame analysis.

The panel again blamed extreme resource demands for shutting down the Sora video generator in March, saying customers mainly wanted coding models and agents. OpenAI didn't rule out bringing it back later.

Because these agents run on their own virtual computers and AI-generated code is growing fast, demand for traditional processor power is rising too. To cut CPU load, OpenAI has a dedicated team that combs through its internal codebases every week.

OpenAI wants developers locked into its platform, not just its models

Beyond the individual product updates, the event showed how tightly OpenAI wants to lock developers and businesses into its ecosystem. With the Agents API, OpenAI runs the agent infrastructure itself. Plugins and web apps give developers more ways to offer their own products on its platform.

The pitch is less technical work and access to what OpenAI says are 1.2 billion weekly ChatGPT users. The model looks a lot like earlier app stores. Developers build the apps, and OpenAI supplies the infrastructure and distribution channel.

Keeping the underlying runtime, Codex Harness, open source doesn't undercut this strategy. Developers can read the code and run it themselves. But anyone who relies on managed services, platform-specific integrations, and finding customers through ChatGPT will likely have a hard time switching ecosystems later.

So the message in Berlin wasn't only that the models keep getting better. OpenAI wants developers to build their businesses directly on its infrastructure.

translation.html:
在柏林举行的 DevDay Exchange 2026 活动上，OpenAI 主要重申了此前已在旧金山公布的消息。关于 Dots 在欧洲的推出、Codex 的使用情况以及问答环节，活动披露了一些新细节。

OpenAI 开发者体验负责人 Romain Huet 表示，在与监管机构沟通后，AI 助手 Dots 应该会在“几周内”向欧洲更多用户开放。欧洲经济区、瑞士和英国的个人 Pro 账户仍无法使用这项服务。部分企业账户已经可以获得访问权限。

据 OpenAI 称，自 2026 年 1 月以来，德国的 Codex 周活跃用户数已增至原来的二十倍。早在 6 月，我们就曾根据该公司自己的数据，报道过用户数增至原来的七倍以上。OpenAI 此次仍未公布绝对数字。该公司表示，近五分之一的桌面端用户会使用文档、演示文稿或电子表格技能，这意味着他们正在用这款编程工具处理日常办公事务。

在问答环节，有人问，为什么 OpenAI 至今仍未提供像 Google 的 Gemini 那样能够理解视频序列的模型。管理层表示，客户几乎没有提出过这方面的需求。因此，除单帧分析外，该公司尚未优先推进这项功能。

讨论嘉宾再次将原因归结为极高的资源需求，以此解释为何在 3 月关闭 Sora 视频生成器，并表示客户主要需要的是编程模型和智能体。OpenAI 没有排除日后恢复该服务的可能性。

由于这些智能体在各自的虚拟计算机上运行，而且 AI 生成的代码正迅速增多，对传统处理器算力的需求也在上升。为降低 CPU 负载，OpenAI 设有一个专门团队，每周梳理其内部代码库。

OpenAI 希望将开发者锁定在其平台上，而不只是让他们使用其模型

除了各项产品更新，这场活动还展现了 OpenAI 希望将开发者和企业牢牢绑定在自身生态系统中的意图。通过 Agents API，OpenAI 自行运行智能体基础设施。插件和 Web 应用则为开发者提供了更多途径，让他们能在其平台上提供自己的产品。

其卖点是减少技术工作，并触达 OpenAI 所称的 12 亿 ChatGPT 周活跃用户。这种模式与早期的应用商店颇为相似。开发者构建应用，OpenAI 则提供基础设施和分发渠道。

将底层运行时 Codex Harness 保持开源，并不会削弱这一策略。开发者可以阅读代码并自行运行。但任何依赖托管服务、平台专属集成以及通过 ChatGPT 寻找客户的人，日后很可能都难以切换到其他生态系统。

因此，柏林这场活动传递的信息并不只有模型在不断进步。OpenAI 希望开发者直接在其基础设施上构建自己的业务。
